senses.definition: (UK law) Someone who commits buggery; a sodomite.
examples: The British Sexual Offences Act of 1967 is a buggers’ charter.

senses.definition: (slang, derogatory, Commonwealth, Hawaii) A foolish or worthless person or thing; a despicable person.
examples: He's a silly bugger for losing his keys.
The bugger’s given me the wrong change.
My computer's being a bit of a bugger.

1928, Frank Parker Day, Rockbound, Gutenberg Australia eBook #0500721h,
“I’ll take it out on dat young bugger,” he thought viciously.

quotes.text: Here the cheers and shouts of the gallery were interrupted by a shabby little man in the back row who yelled out with piercing distinctness: “Don't matter what you call ’im now, George. The bugger’s dead.”

senses.definition: (slang, Commonwealth, Hawaii) A situation that is aggravating or causes dismay; a pain.
examples: So you're stuck out in the woop-woop and the next train back is Thursday next week. Well, that's a bit of a bugger.

senses.definition: (slang, Commonwealth, Hawaii) Someone viewed with affection; a chap.
examples: How are you, you old bugger?

1946, Olaf Stapledon, Arms Out of Hand, in Collected Stories, Gutenberg Australia eBook #0601341,
Good luck, you old bugger!

1953 February-March, Henry Beam Piper, John Joseph McGuire, Null-ABC, in Astounding Science Fiction, Gutenberg eBook #18346,
“And if Pelton found out that his kids are Literates—Woooo!” Cardon grimaced. “Or what we've been doing to him. I hope I’m not around when that happens. I’m beginning to like the cantankerous old bugger.”

senses.definition: (slang, dated) A damn, anything at all.
examples: I don't give a bugger how important you think it is.

senses.definition: (slang, Commonwealth) Someone who is very fond of something
examples: I'm a bugger for Welsh cakes.

senses.definition: (slang, UK, US) A whippersnapper, a tyke.
examples: What is that little bugger up to now?

senses.definition: To have anal sex with, sodomize.
examples: To be buggered sore like a hobo's whore (Attributed to Harry Mclintock's 1920s era Big Rock Candy Mountain)
This computer is buggered! Oh no! I've buggered it up.

senses.definition: (slang) Expressing contemptuous dismissal of the grammatical object.
examples: Bugger Bognor. (Alleged to be the last words of King George V of the United Kingdom in response to a suggestion that he might recover from his illness and visit Bognor Regis.)
Oh, bugger this! I'm going out for a beer instead.

senses.definition: (slang, British, Ireland, Commonwealth, vulgar) An expression of annoyance or displeasure.

quotes.text: Dear Lord, forgive me for what I am about to, ah, say in this magnificent place of worship. Bugger. Bugger! Bugger-bugger-bugger-bugger!
